rationale.complete: Round 1 done in two layers: replication on all 33 eligible kickoffs (per-period READMEs and an NE34 cross-kickoff folder) plus four period-native tests (G51 private goals with NE38, G44, G38, G26). Synthetic validation came first and led to Amendment 1; post hoc robustness checks (echo removal, DQ5 style residualization, chat-only, leave-one-period-out) are labelled. Five of the six variants HH179-HH184 were tested. The confirmatory script is written and dry-run, not run. Not done: embedding swap, #12 native, settling time, causal HH181.
rationale.faithfulness: The core claim holds strongly on exploration data. The day-1 centroid identifies its own kickoff against strong nulls (swap with genericness correction, within-regime and neighbouring decoys, the previous state, echo removal, style) and fails only where the text names no shared target. #51 agents land on their own goal texts (0.95), and NE38 is a clean intervention. The frozen projects are the goal-named ones, and carry-over is rejected. But the specificity half (P3), the two-domain, family and plan variants all failed, P2 is mixed by its literal rule, there is one embedding model, and the holdout was not run. Scorecard A1 B1 C2 D1 E1 F1 G2 H1 I1.
rationale.usefulness: A real design rule with an intervention behind it: day-1 content lands on what the kickoff names, #51 agents land on their own private goals (0.95), and Opus 5's 07-29 reassignment moved it onto its new goal within a day (DiD +0.61); frozen projects carry the goal's name. Not holdout-tested, and text specificity does not set spread. Calibrated 3.5 -> 3.0, the highest usefulness so far.

one_line: Day-1 content lands on its own kickoff (top-1 in 18/33; failures only where no shared target is named), #51 agents land on their own private goals (0.95), frozen projects carry the goal's name; text specificity does not set the spread
